page: The Microsoft Azure DC2as_v5 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCASv5 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 1 physical core that presents 2 dedicated vCPUs through simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB, yielding a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance type contains no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage for disk operations.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized for moderate single-thread efficiency but constrained in aggregate parallel capacity. Single-core evaluations place the instance in the middle tier of general cloud benchmarks, recording a stress-ng single-core score of 1957.91 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1190.0. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics rank lower across tests due to the two-thread limit, as seen in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1441.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2375.45, and a PassMark memory score of 1419.7. Data-handling metrics mirror this profile, with PassMark database operations reaching 709.47 and Redis SET throughput recording 1.68 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC2as_v5 minimizes compute overhead by offering dedicated AMD EPYC execution slices without the expense of larger multi-core nodes or onboard NVMe controllers. The primary tradeoff is the strict ceiling on parallel computation, I/O-intensive database transactions, and memory bandwidth. It functions most effectively as a compute host for low-concurrency workloads, including microservices, continuous integration agents, lightweight backend services, and staging or development environments.
description: Microsoft Azure DC2as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a single physical core providing two dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, the instance includes 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage volumes, and does not include GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments show midrange single-core capabilities, achieving 1190.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1957.91 in stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput is strictly limited by the low core count, resulting in modest PassMark CPU scores of 2375.45 and Redis throughput of 1.68 million operations per second. With its entry-level resource allocation and dedicated compute threads, the DC2as_v5 provides a cost-efficient foundation for lightweight application hosting, microservices, staging environments, and low-traffic web serving.
